bihar_raw_news.title: 'Nitish Setu' conceptualised in 2012, named with consensus in honour of JD(U) chief
bihar_raw_news.content: 'Nitish Setu' conceptualised in 2012, named with consensus in honour of JD(U) chief: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary ANI | Updated: Nov 15, 2026 14:42 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [India], November 15 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Sunday asserted that the infrastructure project 'Nitish Setu' is deeply tied to the vision and legacy of former Chief Minister and JD(U) leader Nitish Kumar. "It was conceptualised by Nitish Kumar in 2012. DPR started being prepared in 2012 itself and before the 2015 elections, its foundation stone was laid. So, with a consensus, this has been named as such in his honour," he said. Earlier, Choudhary announced that the 19.76-kilometre-long six-lane corridor connecting Patna and Vaishali districts, scheduled to be inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 21, would be named in honour of the JD(U) chief. Meanwhile, Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) MP Manoj Kumar Jha raised questions regarding the timing and political haste of such honours, highlighting that trains have been named after a living person. He also pointed out that the relationship Nitish Kumar shares with Lalu Prasad Yadav and the party is something BJP will never attain, even if it remains in power for the next five decades. “Do not view this merely as a political statement from him (Tejashwi Yadav). He has worked with Nitish Kumar, and the relationships Nitish ji shares with Lalu ji and our party are such that even if the BJP remains in power for 50 years, it will not have those relationships," he said. He added, "What surprises me is that, in recent years, a stadium has been named after a person while he is still alive, and trains have also been named after him. There was a tradition of waiting until a person passed away, irrespective of whether they held a position or not. Why have we stopped waiting? What does this haste indicate? History will assess it.” His remarks came after Yadav on Saturday criticised the ruling National Democratic Alliance government over its decision to name the newly constructed six-lane Kachi Dargah–Bidupur Ganga bridge ‘Nitish Setu’ after former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, alleging that the move signals the end of the veteran leader's active political relevance. Speaking to ANI, he said, "It is their government; they can name it whatever they please. They may have named it 'Nitish Setu', but in a way, they have also finished off Nitish Kumar. Usually, such names are given—or statues are erected—in memory of those who are no longer with us. Yet, in this case, the naming has been done while he is still alive. It is as if they are sending a message that, politically, Nitish Kumar is already finished." Naming the Kachi Dargah–Bidupur six-lane bridge ‘Nitish Setu’ marks the first time a landmark public infrastructure project in Bihar has been officially named after him, occurring after he stepped down as Chief Minister. bihar_raw_news.title: JDU's Shyam Rajak hits back at opposition to naming new Bihar bridge after Nitish Kumar
bihar_raw_news.content: National JDU’s Shyam Rajak hits back at opposition to naming new Bihar bridge after Nitish Kumar On Nov 15, 2026 Share Patna, Nov 15 (IANS) Janta Dal-United’s national General Secretary Shyam Rajak on Sunday hit back at Rashtriya Janata Dal supremo Lalu Prasad Yadav’s daughter Rohini Acharya over her objection to a bridge being named after former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, invoking the fodder and bitumen scams to target the party leadership. Taking a swipe at Lalu Prasad’s daughter for demanding that the newly constructed six-lane Kacchi Dargah Raghopur-Bidupur Ganga bridge should be named after her father or as the ‘Social Justice Bridge’, Rajak said that if the state were to be named after political figures, it could also be named after scandals associated with their tenure. “According to them, the entire state of Bihar should be renamed Charanagar. There was the fodder scam and the bitumen scam; a state should be named Bitumen Scam State, or another should be named Fodder Scam State,” he said. He alleged that those who were known for corruption had forgotten the condition of Bihar before 2005 and defended Nitish Kumar’s contribution to the state’s development. “If people who were only known for their corruption speak like this, then probably they have forgotten Bihar before 2005. Our leader, respected Nitish Kumar ji, took charge of a dilapidated Bihar and worked to transform it into a developed and respected state,” he said. Rajak maintained that naming the bridge after Nitish Kumar was not merely an honour for the former Chief Minister but also recognition of the state and its people. “This is not about honouring Nitish Kumar; this is about honouring the entire state, and its people. The bridge is a symbol of remembering a person who, irrespective of their caste, creed, background, religion, and gender, took the people towards better conditions. That person is Nitish Kumar,” he added. Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced the newly constructed six-lane bridge would be renamed as ‘Nitish Setu ‘ after the JD-U President, which the family of veteran leader and RJD chief Lalu Prasad Yadav has opposed. In a post on X, Choudhary said Prime Minister Narendra Modi would dedicate the bridge to the nation during his visit to Bihar on November 21. The Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur bridge project, built at a cost of more than Rs 5,000 crore, is a major infrastructure project connecting North and South Bihar. The state government secured a loan of Rs 3,000 crore from the Asian Development Bank, while the remaining Rs 2,000 crore was funded through its own resources. The decision to construct the bridge was taken in 2015, and its foundation stone was laid in 2016. –IANS sud/vd Share Facebook Twitter Google+ ReddIt WhatsApp Pinterest Email

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Kharna marks the beginning of 36-hour-long fast - Newsonair
bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | November 14, 2026 8:02 PM Bihar: Kharna marks the beginning of 36-hour-long fast On the second day of Chhath Mahaparv, devotees across Bihar today performed the Kharna ritual. With this, the 36-hour-long fast without food and water has begun. After observing a day-long fast, devotees performed prayers in the evening and partook of prasad consisting of jaggery kheer, roti and bananas. Traditionally, the prasad is prepared on a clay stove using mango wood as fuel, with holy Ganga water used in its preparation. With the consumption of the Kharna prasad, devotees have now begun their 36-hour-long Nirjala fast, during which they abstain from both food and water. From a nutritional perspective, the traditional ingredients used in Kharna prasad provide energy that helps the body sustain itself during the prolonged fast. Tomorrow morning, women in households will collectively begin preparing the traditional Thekua prasad. In the evening, devotees will offer Arghya to the setting Sun. The festival will conclude on Monday with the offering of Arghya to the rising Sun. Meanwhile, elaborate arrangements have been made at river ghats, ponds and specially created water bodies across the state for devotees to offer prayers to the Sun God. The ghats and surrounding pathways have been beautifully decorated with colourful rangolis and illuminated with lights. The administration has also made extensive arrangements at various locations to ensure the convenience and safety of devotees.

national_raw_news.title: Logo and mascot for 8th edition of Khelo India Youth Games unveiled 3 hours ago 62
national_raw_news.content: Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya and Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy today unveiled the logo and mascot for the 8th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games. The Games will be held across six cities in Telangana from 11th to 22nd of next month. Addressing the gathering, Dr Mandaviya said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has placed special emphasis on connecting the youth with sports and making sports an integral part of the country’s development vision. He said various sporting events, including the Khelo India Youth Games, Khelo India Beach Games, Winter Games and Tribal Games, are being organised under the Khelo India initiative to encourage greater participation of young people in sports. Speaking on the occasion, Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy said events such as the Khelo India Youth Games would help advance the Prime Minister’s vision of a Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat by encouraging young people to stay away from substance abuse and other social challenges. Both Dr Mandaviya and Mr Reddy expressed their gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his guidance and support in organising the Khelo India Youth Games in Telangana. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said around eight thousand athletes and participants are expected to take part in the Games. The 8th edition will feature 29 disciplines, including 27 competitive sports and two demonstration events.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, the mantra of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’ had instilled new self-confidence among the poor, enabling crores of people to overcome poverty. Mr Modi was addressing the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme at Gadchiroli in Maharashtra, through video conferencing as part of the nationwide celebrations marking the 151st birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The Prime Minister said the government has devoted special attention and resources to the most backward tribal regions, which lacked basic amenities. He said over one lakh crore rupees had been allocated for the PM-JANMAN Yojana and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan. Mr Modi said Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, which was first observed on 15th November 2021, has now become a national celebration. He said there was a time when many national occasions and festivals were viewed through a foreign perspective, but today, India is remembering its heritage, history and heroes with a sense of pride and self-respect. He described this as a significant shift in the country’s national consciousness. The Prime Minister said two major achievements of the country are being widely discussed. He said nearly 50 crore people have overcome extreme poverty, while the country has also made significant progress in eliminating Naxalism and Maoist violence. Mr Modi said the government has placed special emphasis on regions that have lagged behind in development for a long time. Special campaigns have been launched across more than 100 Aspirational Districts and 500 Aspirational Blocks, including areas with significant tribal populations. He added that, under the PM Krishi Dhan-Dhaanya Yojana, special attention is being given to 100 districts that are lagging behind in the agricultural sector. Referring to a recent World Bank report stating that nearly 50 crore Indians had moved out of extreme poverty over the past 12 to 13 years, the Prime Minister described it as one of India’s major achievements since Independence. He said this progress was the result not of any single government but of the collective efforts of society, the hard work of citizens and targeted government initiatives, including schemes and measures for tribal welfare. Mr Modi also interacted with selected tribal beneficiaries during the programme. On the occasion, the Prime Minister inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 246 development projects worth around three thousand crore rupees. The projects aim to strengthen education, healthcare, livelihoods and community infrastructure for tribal communities across the country. He inaugurated 173 projects, including 38 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) for tribal students and 100 Multipurpose Centres under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN). These centres will serve as hubs for service delivery and community activities. The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones for 19 new Eklavya Model Residential Schools and 12 Tribal Multipurpose Marketing Centres (TMMCs). In addition, he inaugurated and launched several other projects under PM-JANMAN and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan, and laid the foundation stones for 42 projects under the two initiatives. Mr Modi also inaugurated the Tribal Research Institute building at Itanagar in Arunachal Pradesh, and the Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighters’ Museum in Mizoram. These facilities aim to preserve and promote tribal culture and heritage. The programme marked the culmination of Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada, observed across the country from the 1st to the 15th of November. Union Tribal Affairs Minister Jual Oram and Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis also addressed the gathering in Gadchiroli.

national_raw_news.title: ASEAN Summit: Philippine President calls for greater regional unity to address geopolitical tens...
national_raw_news.content: The 49th ASEAN Summit began in Manila this morning, with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. calling for greater regional unity and collective action to address geopolitical tensions, economic uncertainties and security challenges. Addressing regional leaders during the opening ceremony, Marcos stressed the importance of strengthening cooperation to safeguard peace, stability and prosperity across Southeast Asia. He underscored the need for ASEAN member states to work together in responding to emerging regional and global challenges. Hosted by the Philippines under the theme “Navigating Our Future, Together,” the three-day summit brings together ASEAN leaders and dialogue partners to discuss key issues, including regional security, economic cooperation, maritime affairs and connectivity. India is also set to have a significant presence at the summit, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi scheduled to visit the Philippines from November 16 to 17. During his visit, Modi will participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit on November 17. His participation is expected to further strengthen India’s Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with ASEAN and expand cooperation in trade, investment, maritime security and regional connectivity. The Summit is scheduled to conclude on November 17, with the Philippines set to hand over the ASEAN chairmanship to Singapore.

national_raw_news.title: Indian markets continue winning streak for third consecutive week due to strong FII inflows 14 Nov 2026 | 3:30 PM 823
national_raw_news.content: Indian stock market extended its gaining streak for the third consecutive week, supported by strong foreign institutional investor (FII) inflows and better-than-expected corporate earnings. However, rising retail inflation, elevated US Treasury yields, rupee weakness and uncertainty surrounding the global monetary policy outlook limit the pace of gains. The 30-share Sensex at the Bombay Stock Exchange climbed 564 points, or 0.7 per cent, to close at 81 thousand 592. The National Stock Exchange Nifty 50 gained 114 points, or nearly half a per cent to end at 25 thousand and 144. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, Midcap 100 index soared 2.1 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index surged 3.6 per cent during the week. On the sectoral front, the Nifty PSU Bank index emerged as the top performer, surging 7.5 per cent over the week. The Nifty Media index advanced 5.2 per cent, while the Nifty Capital Markets index gained 3.8 per cent. In contrast, the Nifty IT index was the weakest performer among the major sectoral indices, declining 3.2 per cent, while the Nifty Cement index slipped 2.1 per cent. Investor wealth on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) witnessed a significant uptick this week, with the combined market capitalisation of all listed companies surging by over 7 lakh crore rupees. In the forex market, the Indian rupee depreciated by 34 paise this week to settle at 94 rupees and 25 paise against the US dollar.

national_raw_news.content: India and Egypt today agreed to work towards finalising the Terms of Reference (ToR) for a proposed bilateral trade agreement to strengthen economic ties between the two countries. At the 7th India-Egypt Joint Trade Committee meeting in Cairo, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said, the two countries could enhance cooperation in several sectors, including pharmaceuticals and healthcare, engineering and automobiles, agriculture, digitisation, fintech and museums. Highlighting opportunities for cooperation in the fintech sector, Mr Goyal said the central banks of both countries were working to promote trade in local currencies. He also proposed linking India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) with Egypt’s digital payment systems. The Minister said a joint team from both countries would work in a time-bound manner to finalise the Terms of Reference for the proposed trade agreement. He said the agreement could take bilateral economic relations to a new level by expanding trade and investment and promoting a more comprehensive partnership across various sectors, including education. The Egyptian delegation was led by Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt. Mr Goyal arrived in Cairo yesterday on a two-day visit aimed at strengthening India-Egypt relations and expanding trade, investment and industrial cooperation. A delegation of more than 130 business leaders and start-ups is accompanying him.

national_raw_news.title: Audience to enjoy Soviet-era musical classic as Russia is Partner country of IFFI 2026 55 mins ago 18
national_raw_news.content: Russia has been named the Partner Country for the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026, which will be held in Goa from the 20th to the 28th of this month. As part of the special showcase, the festival will present a curated selection of four Russian films, featuring contemporary productions alongside a celebrated Soviet-era musical classic. The four films are Bo Bo, directed by Anastasia Kuzina; Sidney Lumet’s Birthday, directed by Raul Geidarov; New Home, directed by Nikita Grushin; and Cheryomushki, directed by Herbert Rappaport. Bo Bo is a poignant rural drama exploring themes of identity, acceptance and prejudice. Through the story of Nadia, a young girl who faces ridicule because of a facial haemangioma, the film portrays her journey towards self-expression through music. It highlights the importance of overcoming societal prejudice rather than changing one’s appearance. Winner of the Grand Jury Prize at the Vyborg National Film Festival, Sidney Lumet’s Birthday is a coming-of-age drama centred on 17-year-old Dato. The film explores family tensions, abandonment and forgiveness as Dato navigates difficult relationships and confronts generational wounds. New Home is a drama about second chances and redemption. It follows Anna, who struggles to rebuild her life after spending seven years in prison, with support from social services and Roman. The film explores the challenges of social reintegration, healing and confronting the past to make a fresh start. Cheryomushki, directed by Herbert Rappaport, is a musical satire set in post-war Moscow. Revolving around four young couples aspiring to own better homes, the film uses music, choreography and humour to highlight bureaucratic corruption while celebrating community spirit and solidarity. Through this specially curated selection, IFFI 2026 seeks to reaffirm the enduring cultural ties between India and Russia while providing audiences with an opportunity to explore the diversity and evolving expressions of Russian cinema.

national_raw_news.title: WAVES Film Bazaar aims to connect South Asian cinema with international markets and audiences 36 mins ago 12
national_raw_news.content: WAVES Film Bazaar, one of the region’s leading platforms for cinematic exchange, collaboration and business opportunities, will hold its 20th edition in Goa from the 20th to the 24th of this month, alongside the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026. Organised by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, WAVES Film Bazaar aims to connect South Asian cinema with international markets and audiences by bringing together filmmakers, producers, financiers, distributors, sales agents and festival programmers. The key initiatives include the Co-Production Market, which connects selected feature films and documentaries with international producers and financiers; the NFDC Screenwriters’ Lab, which nurtures emerging writing talent; and the Work-in-Progress Lab, which provides expert feedback to filmmakers. The Viewing Room, Market Screenings and Producers’ Lab will further facilitate industry networking, project development and opportunities to connect with potential buyers and distributors. The Knowledge Series will bring together industry leaders to discuss emerging trends, distribution strategies, business models and international collaborations. Country and state pavilions, technology showcases and market stalls will also provide opportunities to promote cross-border partnerships and highlight developments in the global audiovisual industry. Initiated by NFDC in 2007 to promote South Asian storytelling, Film Bazaar has contributed to the journey of several acclaimed films, including The Lunchbox, Court, Newton, Manto, Girls Will Be Girls and Cactus Pears, among others. NFDC has also extended financial support to more than 300 films across 21 regional languages, many of which have received national and international recognition. Marking two decades of its journey, the 20th edition of WAVES Film Bazaar aims to strengthen India’s presence in the global film ecosystem by supporting emerging filmmakers, encouraging creative partnerships and creating new opportunities for Indian cinema on the international stage.

national_raw_news.title: Devotees offer Arghya to setting Sun amid mesmerising atmosphere of faith and devotion 47 mins ago 167
national_raw_news.content: Devotees across Bihar offered Sandhya Arghya to the setting Sun today on the third day of Chhath Mahaparv. Chhath ghats across the state witnessed a sea of devotees as people gathered along riverbanks, ponds and other water bodies to perform the traditional rituals with religious fervour and devotion. “Om Ehi Surya Sahasransho Tejorashe Jagatpate, Anukampaya Mam Bhaktya Grihanarghyam Divakar.” With the chanting of this Vedic mantra and deep devotion more than 10,000 ghats across Bihar witnessed, lack of devotees offering Sandhya arghya to the setting Sun on the third day of Chhath Maha Parv. Devotees arrived at the Ganga, Son, PunPun and other river ghats with their family members, carrying traditional bamboo baskets known as Daura and Soop filled with fruits, Thekua and other offerings. They offered Arghya to the setting Sun and prayed for the prosperity, good health and well-being of their families. The air resonated with traditional Chhath songs and devotional chants dedicated to Chhathi Maiya and the Sun God. The glow of earthen lamps along the banks of the Ganga, combined with the crimson hues of the setting Sun, created a mesmerising atmosphere of faith and devotion. The administration has made extensive arrangements at Chhath ghats across the state to ensure the convenience and safety of devotees. Boats, divers and SDRF teams have been deployed. Now, Devotees will offer the second Arghya to the rising Sun tomorrow morning. This will be followed by the Paran of the 36-hour-long fast, marking the conclusion of the four-day Chhath Mahaparv.

national_raw_news.title: HM Amit Shah sets December 2027 deadline to restart NHEC plant in Pune 1 hour ago 27
national_raw_news.content: Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah today announced that production at the revived National Heavy Engineering Cooperative Limited at Pune in Maharashtra, is expected to begin before December 2027. He said the facility will manufacture machinery for sugar factories, dairy equipment, and machinery required for ethanol and Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG) projects. The initiative is expected to reduce dependence on imports, promote indigenous manufacturing, generate employment and boost exports. Mr Shah was speaking after laying the foundation stone of the National Heavy Engineering Cooperative Limited, inaugurating the Regional Office of the Registrar of Cooperative Societies and launching the Bharat Taxi service in Pune He said the cooperative institution, spread over 110 acres, had earlier supplied machinery to sugar factories in India and several other countries. Following its closure, the Union Cooperation Ministry took the initiative to revive the institution with investments from the National Dairy Development Board, Amul, IFFCO, NCDC, NAFED and other cooperative organisations. The revived facility will manufacture equipment for the sugar, dairy, power generation, ethanol and CBG sectors. Plans are also underway to manufacture equipment for the railway and defence sectors, besides containers for exports. Mr Shah said the project will promote a circular economy by ensuring the optimum utilisation of resources generated through sugar production and creating additional income opportunities for farmers. Speaking about Bharat Taxi, Mr Shah said it was a cooperative initiative owned by drivers, aimed at protecting them from exploitation by private taxi aggregators. He said the entire fare amount would be transferred directly to drivers’ bank accounts without any commission deductions. The service has been launched in Mumbai, Nashik and Pune and will be expanded to other cities across the country. Union Minister of State for Cooperation Murlidhar Mohol described the revival of the engineering cooperative, inauguration of the regional office and expansion of Bharat Taxi as significant milestones for the cooperative sector. He also highlighted the computerisation of 80,000 Primary Agricultural Credit Societies across the country. Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde said the revival of the institution, which had remained closed for nearly 11 years, was a matter of pride for the state. He expressed confidence that the project would generate thousands of employment opportunities and strengthen the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. Mr Shah also planted a sapling under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will participate in the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, today through video conferencing. The programme marks the 151st birth anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. During the programme, the Prime Minister will inaugurate and lay the foundation stones of 246 development projects worth around three thousand crore rupees. These projects aim to strengthen education, healthcare, livelihoods and community infrastructure for tribal communities across the country. Besides, PM Modi will inaugurate 173 projects, including 38 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) for tribal students and 100 Multi-Purpose Centres. These centres come under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) and will serve as hubs for service delivery and community activities. The Prime Minister will also lay the foundation stones of 19 new Eklavya Model Residential Schools and 12 Tribal Multipurpose Marketing Centres (TMMCs). He will inaugurate various other projects under PM-JANMAN and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA). In addition, he will lay the foundation stones of 42 other projects under PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA. PM Modi will also inaugurate the Tribal Research Institute (TRI) building in Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh, and the Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighter Museum in Mizoram. These initiatives aim to preserve tribal culture and heritage. The programme will mark the culmination of Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada, being observed across the country from the 1st to the 15th of this month.

national_raw_news.title: Men’s U-19 Asia Cup: India defeat Pakistan to clinch title for ninth time
national_raw_news.content: In Men’s Cricket, India defeated Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling final to clinch the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup title in Muscat, Oman, today. Lower-order batters Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva played sensational knocks to help India snatch victory from the jaws of defeat and successfully chase down a challenging target of 338 runs. Needing three runs off the final delivery, Mohit Ulva struck a boundary to seal India’s record-extending ninth title. Mohit remained unbeaten on 49 off just 26 deliveries, while Manal Chauhan contributed a valuable 47 off 32 balls. Skipper Lakshya Raichandani also played a crucial role with a brilliant 80-run knock. Mohit Ulva was named player of the match, while Aaryavir Sehwag was awarded player of the tournament. Earlier, opting to bat first, Pakistan posted 337 for 9 in their allotted 50 overs. Their innings was powered by a century from Usman Khan and half-centuries from Abdul Qadir and Farhan Yousaf. For India, Kavya Patel led India’s bowling attack, claiming four wickets. President Droupadi Murmu congratulated Team India on winning the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup. In a social media post, the President lauded the young champions for displaying exceptional skill, determination, and composure throughout the closely contested final match. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has also congratulated the young cricketers. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that today is an outstanding day for Indian cricket. He said that their success will inspire several youngsters. Congratulating young cricketers, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said that the determination, firm resolve, and excellent sportsmanship they demonstrated on the pitch were a masterclass in India’s cricketing excellence.

national_raw_news.title: India must become developer, innovator, global leader in advanced technologies - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: India must become developer, innovator, global leader in advanced technologies: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर India must become developer, innovator, global leader in advanced technologies: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh ANI | Updated: Nov 15, 2026 14:03 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 15 (ANI): Union Minister Rajnath Singh has called for making India not merely a user of advanced technologies, but also a developer, innovator and global leader in critical domains, emphasising the need to strengthen the country’s Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) ecosystem to enhance defence preparedness and self-reliance. According to the Ministry of Defence, virtually addressing the 36th Annual Conference on Non-Destructive Evaluation & Enabling Technologies and the 15th International Symposium on Non-Destructive Testing in Aerospace on November 15, 2026, he stressed the importance of developing indigenous capabilities in advanced inspection technologies, promoting consistent quality assurance practices and ensuring the accuracy, reliability and integrity of testing results, particularly in strategic applications. He asserted that there can be no compromise on the integrity of testing results in strategic applications. “We must strengthen our indigenous capabilities in advanced inspection technologies, specialised sensors, evaluation equipment and associated software. Developing domestic capabilities in these areas is essential for reducing technological dependencies and securing critical defence supply chains. We must promote consistent quality assurance practices across the entire defence industrial ecosystem. Public Sector Undertakings, private manufacturers, start-ups and MSMEs have an important role to play in this endeavour. We must ensure that inspection results are accurate, reliable and traceable, and are based on robust procedures and appropriate standards followed by assessment by qualified professionals,” said the Defence Minister. Rajnath Singh stressed that NDT technologies enable examination of the integrity of materials, components and structures without causing any damage to them. Elucidating the concept, he said just as ultrasound and X-rays help examine the human body without surgical intervention, NDT techniques enable the detection of internal defects in critical components without dismantling or damaging them. Defence Minister underlined that as Indian defence systems become increasingly sophisticated, every critical material, component, assembly and manufacturing process must meet the highest standards of quality and reliability. “Hidden defects can affect operational availability, increase maintenance requirements, reduce the service life of equipment and, in critical situations, jeopardise mission success. We need to move beyond a culture of merely identifying defects towards actively preventing them by embedding quality at every stage of the manufacturing process,” he said. Singh stressed that the progress of a nation depends not merely on the technologies it develops, but also on the quality, reliability and security of the systems it builds. In defence applications, including missiles, aircraft, naval platforms and spacecraft, quality is not merely a manufacturing requirement but an essential element of operational reliability and national security, he said. Emphasising the strategic significance of the sector, he stated that for a country aspiring to achieve technological leadership, the importance of NDT cannot be overstated. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Rural Development Shivraj Singh Chouhan announces five lakh PMAY-G houses for Odisha 29 lakh women in Odisha become Lakhpati Didis; more support for women entrepreneurs Every panchayat in Odisha to receive up to ₹2 crore for development Balangir agriculture college to be developed as the country’s best institution No eligible poor family in Odisha will be left without a pucca house Solar-powered homes to help rural families cut bills and earn additional income Women entrepreneurs to get loans without guarantees Viksit Bharat–G RAM G scheme to accelerate rural development in Odisha Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 6:41PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today announced five lakh pucca houses for poor families in Odisha under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Gramin. Addressing a state-level program of the scheme in Balangir in the presence of Chief Minister Shri Mohan Charan Majhi. The program also witnessed the foundation stone laying for a new agriculture college in Balangir. Deputy Chief Minister and Agriculture Minister Shri Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo, Panchayati Raj and Drinking Water Minister Shri Ravi Narayan Nayak, Health and Family Welfare Minister Dr Mukesh Mahaling, Member of Parliament Smt Sangeeta Kumari Singh Deo, and local legislators Shri Naveen Kumar Jain, Shri Laxman Bag and Ms Rupa Mishra were among those present. national_raw_news.title: Why India's MSMEs Need Digital Skills to Compete Globally - Analytics Insight
national_raw_news.content: Digital Skills: Driving Growth in India's MSME Sector Business Why India's MSMEs Need Digital Skills to Compete Globally India’s MSMEs are embracing digital skills to improve productivity, access finance and expand exports. Digital literacy, AI adoption and online marketplaces are becoming essential for small businesses competing in global markets. Written By : Akshita Pidiha Reviewed By : Manisha Sharma Published: 15th Nov, 2026 at 12:00 PM Updated: 15th Nov, 2026 at 12:00 PM Overview: Indian MSMEs contribute 31.1% to GDP, 35.4% to manufacturing output and 48.58% to exports, making digital transformation critical for future growth. Press Information Bureau KPMG's 2026 report highlights major workforce gaps, with only 10% formally skilled and 45% of core skills expected to change by 2030. KPMG AI adoption, ONDC, digital finance and government training schemes can help small businesses improve productivity, reach new buyers and strengthen export competitiveness. India's micro, small and medium enterprises are the backbone of the national economy. Government data from January 2026 shows that the sector adds about 31.1% to GDP, 35.4% to manufacturing output and 48.58% to exports. Global buyers now prefer suppliers who can sell online, share order updates quickly and show product quality through data. Many owners still rely on paper records and phone calls, which makes it hard to keep up with this pace. Digital skills have become the foundation for growth, easy credit, and steady export orders. Also Read: Trade and Sustainability Training: Skills for Policy, Business, and Development Roles A Sector Too Large to Leave Behind According to the PIB backgrounder released in June 2026, MSMEs employ more than 38.9 crore people, which makes them the second largest source of jobs after agriculture. Udyam registrations crossed 8.7 crore by June 2026, showing that millions of small units have entered the formal system. Formal status brings access to credit, schemes and public tenders. It also creates a digital footprint, which buyers and banks increasingly check before they place an order or approve a loan. A sector of this size can compete in global markets only when its owners and workers learn to use digital tools with confidence. Also Read: RBI Announces Rs. 25,000 Digital Fraud Relief, Raises MSME Loan Limit to Rs. 20 Lakh Skills Gap that Holds Firms Back KPMG's February 2026 report on MSME talent describes a deep structural gap. Only about 10 % of the MSME workforce has formal skilling, and productivity stands at just 14 % of the level seen in large enterprises. The report also expects 45 % of core skills to change by 2030. Weak digital readiness means that a clerk may not read a dashboard, a supervisor may not log quality data and an owner may not understand an online contract. These gaps slow delivery and raise costs. Global buyers compare suppliers on speed and reliability, so every delay reduces the chance of a repeat order. national_raw_news.content: COAS General Dhiraj Seth departs on an official visit to Czech Republic Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर COAS General Dhiraj Seth departs on an official visit to Czech Republic ANI | Updated: Nov 15, 2026 11:13 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], November 15 (ANI): Chief of the Army Staff (COAS), General Dhiraj Seth, proceeded on an official visit to the Czech Republic from November 16 to 19. The visit aims to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation, enhance military-to-military engagement and explore opportunities for collaboration in defence technology and industry. According to a release from the Ministry of Defence, the COAS will hold discussions with senior military leaders of the Czech Armed Forces, including Lieutenant General Petr Čepelka, First Deputy Chief of the General Staff and the Deputy Chief of Defence at General Staff Headquarters (GSHQ) in Prague during the visit. The COAS will pay tribute to fallen soldiers during a wreath-laying ceremony at the GSHQ. He will call on senior officials of the Ministry of Defence. These engagements will focus on matters of mutual interest, including military cooperation, training, modernisation and emerging security challenges. As part of the programme, General Dhiraj Seth will visit the Defence University in Brno and the NATO Joint Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defence Centre of Excellence to gain insights into specialised training, operational capabilities and future readiness of the Czech Armed Forces. The COAS will interact with representatives of the Inter-governmental Defence Cooperation Agency (AMOS), the Defence and Security Industry Association and leading defence manufacturers to explore opportunities for cooperation in defence technology and industry. The visit reflects the shared commitment of India and the Czech Republic to strengthening bilateral defence relations through sustained military dialogue, professional exchanges and industrial partnerships. This comes a month after Defence Minsiter Rajnath Singh's held a bilateral meeting with the 1st Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Industry and Trade of the Czech Republic, Karel Havlíček, in New Delhi on October 13. During the interaction, both leaders reviewed the entire spectrum of defence industrial cooperation between the two countries. While the two sides welcomed the ongoing collaboration and successful establishment of various joint ventures, they agreed to further expand this cooperation, including under the aegis of India -Czech Joint Defence Committee to promote ‘Make-in- India ' and ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’. Havlíček was on a four-day visit to India in October and held interactions with various ministries, trade representatives and businesses. national_raw_news.content: Sacred relics of Shakyamuni Buddha arrive at Golden Pagoda, Namsai, marking the final phase of exposition in Arunachal Pradesh Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Sacred relics of Shakyamuni Buddha arrive at Golden Pagoda, Namsai, marking the final phase of exposition in Arunachal Pradesh ANI | Updated: Nov 15, 2026 08:14 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 15 (ANI): The Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha arrived at Namsai , Arunachal Pradesh, on Saturday, marking the commencement of the third and final phase of their exposition in the State. Sacred Relics were ceremonially received and enshrined at the Golden Pagoda (Kongmu Kham), one of the prominent centres of Buddhist faith and heritage in eastern Arunachal Pradesh. According to the press release by the Ministry of Culture, the Governor of Arunachal Pradesh, Lt Gen Kaiwalya Trivikram Parnaik (Retd.), received the Sacred Relics at Nalung Helipad in Namsai . He was accompanied by Deputy Chief Minister Chowna Mein, State Ministers, public representatives and religious leaders. Devotees and members of the local community gathered along the ceremonial route to the Golden Pagoda to pay their respects to the Sacred Relics. The exposition was formally inaugurated at the Golden Pagoda following the reception and enshrinement ceremony. The Governor graced the occasion as the Chief Guest. Deputy Chief Minister Chowna Mein, Raghav Prasad Bhatnagar, Director General, International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), venerable members of the Buddhist Sangha and other distinguished guests were present on the occasion. Addressing the gathering, the Governor described the exposition as an occasion of profound spiritual and cultural significance. He observed that the Sacred Relics symbolise the life, enlightenment and timeless teachings of Lord Buddha. The Governor highlighted the relevance of Buddhist teachings in addressing contemporary challenges. He noted that the message of peace, compassion, wisdom and non-violence assumes particular significance at a time when humanity faces conflict, intolerance and violence. He urged people to imbibe these values in their daily lives and contribute to building a society founded on harmony, dignity and mutual respect, the release said. The Governor appreciated the collective efforts of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, the National Museum, New Delhi, the International Buddhist Confederation and all those associated with the exposition. He acknowledged their contribution in bringing the Sacred Relics closer to devotees across Arunachal Pradesh. Deputy Chief Minister Chowna Mein highlighted the rich and diverse Buddhist heritage of Arunachal Pradesh. He underlined the significance of the exposition in a State where Mahayana, Vajrayana and Theravada Buddhist traditions have flourished across generations. He described the arrival of the Sacred Relics at Namsai as a rare opportunity for devotees to offer prayers and reconnect with the teachings of Lord Buddha, the release said. On the occasion, two special exhibitions organised by the National Museum, New Delhi, and the International Buddhist Confederation were inaugurated at the Meditation Centre of the Golden Pagoda.
